const LESSONS=`request|Anatomy of a Web Request|Follow a browser request through naming, transport, encryption and rendering.
http|HTTP|A request carries a method, target and headers; a response adds a status and body.
apis|APIs & JSON|Define a stable contract between a client and a service using structured messages.
latency|Latency vs Throughput|Measure the time for one request separately from the number completed each second.
stateless|Stateless Servers|Keep durable session data outside application processes so any instance can serve a request.
async_concept|Sync vs Async|Choose whether callers should wait for work or receive an acknowledgement and continue.
lb|Load Balancer|Distribute incoming traffic across healthy application instances.
hvscaling|Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling|Compare adding machines with making one machine more powerful.
lbalgos|Load Balancing Algorithms|Compare round robin with routing based on active connections or a stable key.
health|Health Checks|Probe readiness before sending a server production traffic.
autoscale|Auto-scaling|Adjust instance counts with demand while allowing time for new capacity to become ready.
sessions|Session Management|Keep identity and session continuity when requests reach different application instances.
cdn|CDN|Serve cacheable content from locations closer to the people requesting it.
edge_computing|Edge Computing|Move selected computation near clients while keeping data consistency in view.
whycache|Why Caches Exist|Avoid repeating expensive work by reusing a previous result.
cache|Cache|Balance hit rate, memory cost and freshness when serving frequently requested values.
writethrough|Write-Through vs Write-Back|Decide when a cached write must reach durable storage.
invalidation|Cache Invalidation|Choose expiration, deletion or versioned keys to stop serving stale data.
multitier|Multi-Tier Caching|Coordinate browser, edge and application caches without losing sight of freshness.
sqlnosql|SQL vs NoSQL|Choose a data model from access patterns, invariants and scaling requirements.
indexes|Database Indexes|Trade storage and write cost for faster lookups on selected fields.
repl|Database Replication|Maintain copies for read capacity and recovery while considering replication lag.
sharding|Sharding|Partition records across machines using a key that spreads the workload.
conshash|Consistent Hashing|Limit key movement when the set of storage nodes changes.
acid|ACID Transactions|Protect a group of changes with atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.
eventual|Eventual Consistency|Understand what users may observe while replicas are still converging.
queue_concept|Message Queue|Separate accepting work from processing it with a durable buffer.
pubsub|Pub/Sub|Deliver one event to independent subscribers without coupling their implementations.
eventdriven|Event-Driven Architecture|Model business changes as events and make consumers resilient to duplicates.
websockets|WebSockets|Keep a bidirectional connection open for low-latency updates.
webhooks|Webhooks|Notify another service of an event with signed requests and retry rules.
ratelimit|Rate Limiting|Protect capacity by controlling how much work each caller can request.
spof|Single Point of Failure|Find a component whose loss would interrupt the whole request path.
failover|Failover|Move work to a healthy standby while preserving correct ownership.
circuitbreaker|Circuit Breaker|Stop repeatedly calling a failing dependency and probe it before recovery.
retries|Retries & Backoff|Retry transient failures with limits, increasing delays and jitter.
idempotency|Idempotency|Make repeated delivery safe by associating an operation with a stable identifier.
dr|Disaster Recovery|Define recovery time and data-loss targets before choosing backups and replicas.
logging|Logging|Record structured events with context that helps explain a request across services.
metrics|Metrics & Alerting|Track service health through rates, errors, latency and actionable thresholds.
containers|Containers|Package an application and dependencies into a repeatable runtime environment.
cicd|CI/CD|Validate changes in stages and make deployment recoverable.
method|How to Crack a System Design Interview|Clarify requirements, estimate scale, draw a simple system and explore its trade-offs.

 if(mode==='transaction'){limit=rate*(1-knob/100);rejected=Math.round(rate-limit);note='Duplicate keys deduplicated';}
 if(mode==='limit'){limit=knob;rejected=Math.max(0,rate-limit);note=rejected?'Excess requests rate-limited':'Within rate limit';}

 if(mode==='socket'){appCap=live*40/knob;latency=15;}
